questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a metal
questions.solution:
Among all four options, **__Selenium__** is not a metal and it has been named after the Greek goddess of the moon "Selene".

 
• The Selenium belongs to the Non-Metal Category as it is found in Group 16(chalcogens) and Period 4 of the Periodic Table with Atomic number 34.
 
• It was discovered by Jons Jacobs Berzelius in 1817 who was a Swedish Chemist and also considered as one of the founders of Modern Chemistry.
 
• Jacobs Berzelius has also discovered Cerium( Atomic Number-58) lying in the Lanthanide Series of f-block elements.
 
• Selenium resides in the Solid-phase at STP whereas its Melting point is 494K & its Boiling Point is 958K.

questions.question: Five year plan was introduced in India in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**, i.e __**1951**__.

To attain economic growth and prosperity in various spheres, the first five-year plan was introduced in India in __**1951**__.

 
• Though, the First Five year Plan was not based upon any of the well-knitted strategies of long term Planning & Development.
 
• Although, it was focussed on several objectives such as maximum production, full employment, lowering prices, and equality of wealth.
 
• Initially, the **Five-year plans** were developed, promoted, executed as well as monitored by the Planning Commission of India which was established on **15th March 1950**.
 
• There were **Twelve Five Year Plans since 1951** which were presented by **Planning commission** till its dissolution on 17th August 2014 and it was **replaced by National Institution for Transforming India(NITI) Aayog**.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution deals with amendments of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The Part of the constitution which deals with the amendments of the constitution is __**Part-XX**__ of the constitution.

 
• The only Article-368 contained in Part-XX of the Indian Constitution deals with the Power of Parliament & procedure of the amendments in the Constitution.
 
• Till date, the total number of amendments in the constitution is 104 among which the latest one is the amendment of Article 334 on 25th January 2020.
 
• The 42nd amendment act, 1976 is also known as the Mini Constitution of India as it Contained various amendments in Preamble, Fundamental Rights, Legislature etc. as well as Part-IV(A) was also inserted in the constitution of India.

questions.question: Who of the following personalities is known as ‘Loknayak’?
questions.solution:
A great politician and a social worker, __**Jayprakash Narayan**__ is also Known as "LokNayak".

 
• Jayprakash Narayan was Born on 11th October 1902 in Ballia, UP and died on 8th October 1979 in Patna, Bihar.
 
• He went to America for Higher studies and he studied Karl Marx's theory due to which he became Marxist but after returning back to India he joined the Congress party in the influence of Mahatma Gandhi and became a Socialist.
 
• He was awarded Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1965 and posthumously he was awarded the highest civilian award "Bharat Ratan" in 1999.

questions.question: 15th Finance commission is headed by:

• The 15th Finance Commission was constituted with the approval of President of India in November 2017.
 
• The major function of the finance commission is to give suggestions on center-state financial relations.

questions.question: Michael Phelps, the celebrated swimmer belongs to ______.
questions.solution:

questions.question: Mohenjo-daro lies on bank of which river?
questions.solution:
Mohenjo-Daro lies on the bank of the **Indus** river in the Larkana district of Sindh Province of Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: Dronacharya award is associated with ______.
questions.solution:
Dronacharya award is associated with __**Sports**__.

• It was first awarded in 1985 to Bhalchandra Bhaskar Bhagwat.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correct?
questions.solution:
The pair of the "__**Great Himalayan National Park-Himachal Pradesh**__" is Correct.

questions.question: Which of the following text is referred as ‘Vedanta’?
questions.solution:
The __**Upanishads**__ along with Brahamsutra and Bhagavad Gita are referred to as Vedanta or Departures.

 
• The Upanishads are assumed to be the last Source of the Shrutis in Hinduism associated with Vedas.
 
• Upanishads are considered to be the important sources of Indian philosophy and it basically deals with the knowledge of Brahma, Jiva and Jagat.

questions.question: Who among the following was the youngest person to receive a Nobel Prize?
questions.solution:
__**William Lawrence Bragg**__ was the Youngest person to receive a Noble Prize at the age of 25 years in 1915.

 
• He was awarded the Noble prize in physics for the analysis of crystal structure by means of X-Ray.
 
• He belonged to Adelaide, Australia and he is well known for the X-Ray diffraction and Bragg's Equation.

questions.question: What is the symbol of gold?
questions.solution:
The Symbol of GOLD is __**Au**__.

 
• The symbol of Gold has been derived from the Latin term "AURUM"
 
• It is a solid metal that is least reactive in nature.
 
• In the periodic table, Gold is Found in the Group 11 and Period 6 with the Atomic Number 79.
 
• Gold is a relatively rare element found naturally and it is used for the purpose of Jewellery & Coinage.
 
• Before 1971, even the Monetary policies of the countries were also based upon Gold Standard.

questions.question: Which award is often referred to as the ‘Nobel Prize of architecture’?

The __**Pritzker Prize**__ in the field of Architecture is often referred to as the "Nobel Prize of Architecture".

questions.question: World Aids Day is celebrated on:
questions.solution:
World AIDS Day takes place on __**1st December**__ every year to support and boost up the confidence of the people living with HIV-AIDS and also to commemorate the people died due to HIV-AIDS.

 
• World AIDS Day was observed for the first time in 1988 as the first-ever health day over the Globe.
 
• "COMMUNITIES MAKE THE DIFFERENCE" was the world AIDS Day theme for the year 2019.
 
• AIDS stands for the Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome.
 
• AIDS can be tested by the anti-body test or the Nucleic Acid test.

questions.question: The branch of medical science that deals with kidneys is known as:
questions.solution:
The Branch of Medical Science which deals with the Kidneys is known as __**Nephrology**__.

 
• This Branch of Medical Science deals with the care and diagnosis of the disorders and diseases of Kidneys.
 
• This branch also deals with the Dialysis as well as the Kidney Transplantations & Plasma Exchange.
 
• The Branch of Medicine which deals with the study of the Heart and other related cardiovascular diseases is known as Cardiology.
 
• The study of Ear, Nose & Throat in the Field of Medicine & their surgical subspecialty within medicine is called Otorhinolaryngology.
 
• Opthalmology is the Specialized study of diagnosis, treatment as well as Surgery of Human eye and related disorders.

questions.question: Who is the Leader of the House in the Seventeenth Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
At present, the Leader of the House in the seventeenth Lok Sabha(Lower House) is Mr __**Narendra Modi**__.

 
• As per the context of the Indian Constitution, by default, Prime minister is the Leader of the House in Lok Sabha.
 
• As per Article 75, the Prime Minister Shall be appointed by the President where the person must be the leader of the party elected with a majority of votes in General Elections.
 
• The first leader of the House in Lok Sabha was Pt. Jawahar Lal Nehru who assumed the office for the first time on 2ⁿd April 1952.

questions.question: Our national anthem ‘Jana Gana Mana’ has been adopted from which language?
questions.solution:
Our National Anthem "Jana Gana Mana" has been adopted from __**Bengali**__

 
• Our National Anthem was originally written in Bengali by the Famous Noble Laureate Rabindranath Tagore.
 
• Our National Anthem was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of India on 24th January 1950.
 
• It was first Sung publicly on 27th December 1911 at Calcutta Session of the Indian National Congress.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a scheduled language of India
questions.solution:
The __**Rajasthani**__ language is not considered in the list of the scheduled languages in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.

 
• The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution consists of the list of 22 languages.
 
• The scheduled languages are those languages which are included in the schedule Eight of the Indian constitution and termed as the Official languages of the Union.
 
• Initially, 14 languages were included in the Schedule Eight of the Indian Constitution and, later on, 7 more languages were added in various amendments among which the latest one was 92ⁿd Amendment, 2003 which added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili & Santhali.

questions.question: In July 2019, which of the following cities inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List?
questions.solution:
__**Jaipur,**__ a city in Rajasthan has been inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage site list in July 2019.

 
• The city of Jaipur has been planned according to the Prastara Plan of Vastu Shastra i.e- a treatise of traditional Hindu architecture.
 
• It is among one of the most important cities of the medieval period which shows the ancient Hindu, Mughal and Contemporary Western ideas which resulted in the customized layout of the city. 
 
• It has created a difference from other medieval cities with its ordered and a grid-like structure such as broad streets, crossing at right angles, earmarked sites for buildings, Palaces, Havelis, Temples, and Gardens, etc. thus ensuring that a uniform facade is maintained in the city.
